From that night forward, the stars have remained, reminding all who gaze upward that even fleeting beauty, when shared generously, can become immortal.

The thread blazed brilliant against the darkness, becoming the first star.

Enchanted by its beauty, Aethera continued weaving. She pulled thread after thread from her essence, each one dimming her own radiance but illuminating the void. She wove constellations and galaxies, nebulas and cosmic rivers, until the entire universe sparkled with light.

Finally, with her last golden thread, Aethera created the Sun—the brightest star of all. Exhausted and faded, she wrapped herself in the remaining darkness and fell into an eternal sleep.

But her sacrifice was not in vain. From the warmth of her stars, life eventually emerged. And on clear nights, when people gaze upward at the glittering sky, they witness Aethera's masterpiece—a reminder that the greatest acts of creation come from giving pieces of ourselves to illuminate others.
